                                              JORDAN PROPERTY FOR ALGEBRAIC GROUPS AND AUTOMORPHISM
                                             GROUPS OF PROJECTIVE VARIETIES IN ARBITRARY CHARACTERISTIC

                                                                                              FEI HU


                                                  A BSTRACT. We show an analogue of Jordan’s theorem for algebraic groups defined over a field
                                                  k of arbitrary characteristic. As a consequence, a Jordan-type property holds for the automor-
                                                  phism group of any projective variety over k.
arXiv:1804.10946v2 [math.AG] 25 Sep 2018




                                                                                      1. I NTRODUCTION

                                           In 1878, Camille Jordan [Jor78] proved the following remarkable theorem.

                                           Theorem 1.1 (cf. [Jor78]). For any positive integer n, there exists a constant J(n) such that
                                           any finite subgroup Γ of GLn over a field of characteristic zero contains a normal abelian
                                           subgroup A of index ≤ J(n).

                                              However, the above theorem is false for fields of characteristic p > 0 due to the existence
                                           of unipotent elements of finite order. For instance, the group GLn (Fp ) contains arbitrarily
                                           large subgroups of the form SLn (Fpr ) which are simple modulo their centers. Nevertheless, for
                                           any finite subgroup Γ of GLn (k) of order not divisible by char(k), there still exists a normal
                                           abelian subgroup A of Γ with [Γ : A] ≤ J(n) for the same J(n) as in Theorem 1.1 (see
                                           e.g. [BF66, 2.9]). Later, Serre showed that the Cremona group Cr2 (k) of rank 2 over a field
                                           k also has this property (cf. [Ser09, Theorem 5.3]). This motivates us to make the following
                                           definition.

                                           Definition 1.2. Let p a prime number or zero. A group G is called a generalized p-Jordan
                                           group, if there exists a constant J(G), depending only on G, such that every finite subgroup Γ
                                           of G whose order is not divisible by p contains a normal abelian subgroup A of index ≤ J(G).
                                           We also call such a group generalized Jordan if there is no confusion caused (e.g., in practice,
                                           p will always denote the characteristic of the ground field k).

                                              Note that when p = 0, this notion coincides with Popov’s [Pop11, Definition 2.1]. The
                                           above-mentioned results can be reformulated as follows. Both general linear groups GLn (k)
                                           and the Cremona group Cr2 (k) of rank 2 are generalized p-Jordan, where p = char(k). Our
                                           first result below shows that in addition to above, any algebraic group is generalized Jordan.

                                             2010 Mathematics Subject Classification. 14G17, 14L10.
                                             Key words and phrases. positive characteristic, Jordan property, algebraic group.
                                             The author was partially supported by a UBC-PIMS Postdoctoral Fellowship.
                                                                                                 1
2                                             FEI HU

Theorem 1.3. Any algebraic group G defined over a field k of characteristic p ≥ 0 is gener-
alized p-Jordan. Namely, there exists a constant J(G), depending only on G, such that every
finite subgroup Γ of G(k) whose order is not divisible by p contains a normal abelian subgroup
of index ≤ J(G).

Remark 1.4. Even in characteristic zero, Theorem 1.3 is nontrivial and has just been proved
by Meng and Zhang recently (cf. [MZ18, Theorem 1.3]). The main obstruction is that the
Jordan property may not be preserved under group extensions (see e.g. [Pop11, Remark 2.12]
or [Pop14, Example 7]). See also [Zar14] for a counterexample. Note, however, that the
argument in [MZ18] also depends on the Levi decomposition of connected algebraic groups
(cf. [Mos56]), which is not available in prime characteristic (see e.g. [Bri15, Remark 4.9] and
references therein). Our approach is based on the investigation of the Jordan property of quo-
tient groups (see e.g. Lemma 2.2 and Step 2 in the proof of Theorem 1.3).

   Another generalization of Jordan’s theorem to prime characteristic was due to Brauer and
Feit [BF66] by allowing arbitrary finite subgroup Γ of GLn (k) whose order may be divisible
by p > 0. They showed that Γ contains a normal abelian subgroup whose index is bounded by
a constant depending on n as well as the order of the p-Sylow subgroup Γ(p) of Γ. Larsen and
Pink [LP11] has subsequently extended Brauer–Feit [BF66] as follows.

Theorem 1.5 (cf. [LP11, Theorem 0.4]). For any positive integer n, there exists a constant
J ′ (n) such that any finite subgroup Γ of GLn over a field k of characteristic p > 0 contains a
normal abelian p′ -subgroup A of index ≤ J ′ (n) · |Γ(p) |3 .

   Here a finite group is called a p-group (resp. p′ -group) if its order is some power of p (resp.
relatively prime to p). In an analogous way, we introduce the following notion.

Definition 1.6. Let p be a prime number. A group G is called a p-Jordan group, if there exist
constants J ′ (G) and e(G), depending only on G, such that every finite subgroup Γ of G contains
a normal abelian p′ -subgroup A of index ≤ J ′ (G) · |Γ(p) |e(G) .

    Below is our second main result extending Theorem 1.5 to arbitrary algebraic groups.

Theorem 1.7. Any algebraic group G defined over a field k of characteristic p > 0 is p-Jordan.
That is, there are constants J ′ (G) and eG , depending only on G, such that any finite subgroup
Γ of G(k) contains a normal abelian p′ -subgroup A of index ≤ J ′ (G) · |Γ(p) |e(G) .

Remark 1.8. We may think of Theorem 1.7 as a stronger version of Theorem 1.3 in positive
characteristic, if we only care about the existence of those constants (i.e., J(G) and J ′ (G)).
Actually, we will see in Section 3 that our constant J(G) = cG J(n)cG , where cG is the number
of connected components of G and n is the least dimension of a faithful representation of
(G◦ )aff over k; see §2.2 for the meaning of (G◦ )aff . But J ′ (G) is much more complicated and
involved. Also, it will be shown that e(G) = 3(rG + 1)cG , where rG is bounded by the rank of
(G◦ )aff .
             JORDAN PROPERTY FOR ALGEBRAIC GROUPS AND AUTOMORPHISM GROUPS                         3

   In characteristic zero, it has also been proved by Meng and Zhang that the automorphism
group Aut(X) is Jordan for any projective variety X (cf. [MZ18, Theorem 1.6]). In this note,
as a byproduct of our main theorems, we also deduce two Jordan-type properties for automor-
phism groups of projective varieties in arbitrary characteristic.

Theorem 1.9. Let X be a projective variety defined over a field k of characteristic p ≥ 0.
Then there exists a constant JX , depending only on X, such that every finite p′ -subgroup Γ of
Aut(X) contains a normal abelian subgroup A of index ≤ JX .

Theorem 1.10. Let X be a projective variety defined over a field k of characteristic p > 0.
Then there exist constants JX′ and eX , depending only on X, such that every finite subgroup Γ
of Aut(X) contains a normal abelian p′ -subgroup A of index ≤ JX′ · |Γ(p) |eX .

   We also note that in characteristic zero, Prokhorov and Shramov proved that the group
Bir(X) of birational self-maps of any non-uniruled variety X is Jordan (cf. [PS14, Theo-
rem 1.8(ii)]). Assuming the Borisov–Alexeev–Borisov conjecture, which was recently proved
in Birkar’s pioneering work [Bir16], they even showed in [PS16] that Bir(X) is (uniformly)
Jordan for any rationally connected variety X, generalizing Serre’s [Ser09, Theorem 5.3] (the
characteristic zero side). Quite recently, as a consequence of the aforementioned Jordan prop-
erty, Reichstein obtained new low bounds on the essential dimension of a series of finite groups
which was not previously known even for special cases (cf. [Rei18, Theorem 3]). At the end of
our introduction, we raise the following natural question (see also [Ser09, Question 6.1] for a
related question).

Question 1.11. Let Crn (k) be the Cremona group of rank n ≥ 2 defined over a field k of
characteristic p > 0. Then is Crn (k) p-Jordan?

                                       2. P RELIMINARIES

2.1. Two group-theoretic lemmas. We need the following two group-theoretic lemmas which
are quite useful in dealing with (generalized) p-Jordan groups (see Definitions 1.2 and 1.6).
See [Pop11, Lemmas 2.6 and 2.8] and [Pop14, Theorem 3] for related results.

Lemma 2.1. Let G1 and G2 be two groups and G their direct product G1 × G2 .
(1) If G1 and G2 are generalized p-Jordan, then so is G1 × G2 and one can take J(G1 × G2 ) =
    J(G1 )J(G2 ).
(2) If G1 and G2 are p-Jordan, then so is G1 ×G2 and one can take J ′ (G1 ×G2 ) = J ′ (G1 )J ′ (G2 ),
    e(G1 × G2 ) = e(G1 ) + e(G2 ) − 1.

Proof. (1) It follows directly from [Pop14, Theorem 3(2)]. For the sake of completeness, we
present the proof here. Let G denote the direct product G1 × G2 and πi : G → Gi the projection
homomorphism. Let Γ be a finite p′ -subgroup of G. Then Γi := πi (Γ) ≤ Gi contains a normal
abelian subgroup Ai such that
                                       [Γi : Ai ] ≤ J(Gi ).

normal abelian subgroup of Γ of index ≤ J(G1 )J(G2 ) as claimed.
  (2) We need to modify the above proof appropriately. More precisely, using the notation

which proves Lemma 2.1.                                                                                       

Lemma 2.2. Let G be a group and K a finite normal subgroup of G.
(1) Suppose that G is generalized p-Jordan and one of the following conditions holds:
      (i) the order of K is not divisible by p,
     (ii) p > 0 and K has a normal Sylow p-subgroup K(p) .
    Then G/K is generalized p-Jordan and one can take J(G/K) = J(G).
(2) Suppose that G is p-Jordan. Then G/K is p-Jordan and one can take

                       J ′ (G/K) = J ′ (G) · |K(p) |e(G) ,           e(G/K) = e(G).
            JORDAN PROPERTY FOR ALGEBRAIC GROUPS AND AUTOMORPHISM GROUPS                         5

Proof. (1) The first case is easy; see e.g. [Pop11, Lemma 2.6]. We now consider the case that
p > 0 and K(p) is nontrivial. Let Γ be a finite p′ -subgroup of G/K. Let H be the inverse of Γ
in G. Since p ∤ |Γ| by the assumption, K(p) is also a Sylow p-subgroup of H. It follows from
K E H that K(p) is also normal in H. Hence K(p) = H(p) is the normal Sylow p-subgroup of
H. Namely, we have the following exact sequence:
                            1 −→ K/K(p) −→ H/H(p) −→ Γ −→ 1.
By the Schur–Zassenhaus theorem (cf. [Rob96, Theorem 9.1.2]), there is a complement KC
(resp. HC ) of K(p) = H(p) in K (resp. H), which satisfies that K = K(p) ⋊ KC (resp.
H = H(p) ⋊ HC ). (Their theorem also states that all complements are conjugate to each other,
here we do not need this conjugation result though). Then we rewrite the above exact sequence
as follows:
                              1 −→ KC −→ HC −→ Γ −→ 1.
Note that our HC now is a finite p′ -subgroup of G. It follows that there is a normal abelian
subgroup AHC of HC such that [HC : AHC ] ≤ J(G). Let A be the image of AHC in Γ. Then
[Γ : A] ≤ [HC : AHC ] ≤ J(G).
  (2) Let Γ be a finite subgroup of G/K and H the inverse of Γ in G. Then H contains a
normal abelian p′ -subgroup AH of index ≤ J ′ (G) · |H(p) |e(G) . Let A be the image of AH in Γ.
Noting that |H(p) | = |K(p) | · |Γ(p) |, we thus have
           [Γ : A] ≤ [H : AH ] ≤ J ′ (G) · |H(p) |e(G) = J ′ (G) · |K(p) |e(G) · |Γ(p) |e(G) .
This yields the assertion (2) and hence Lemma 2.2 follows.                                       

2.2. Two algebraic group-theoretic theorems. Let G be a connected algebraic group defined
over a perfect field k. We record the following classical decomposition theorem of algebraic
groups. By the Chevalley’s structure theorem, there is a smallest connected normal affine
subgroup scheme Gaff of G such that the quotient G/Gaff is an abelian variety (cf. [Bri17,
Theorem 2]). On the other hand, G has a smallest connected normal subgroup scheme Gant
such that the quotient G/Gant is affine; moreover, Gant is smooth and contained in the center
Z(G) of G (cf. [Ros56, §5]). We have the following Rosenlicht’s decomposition theorem (see
e.g. [Bri17, §5.1]).

Theorem 2.3 (cf. [Bri17, Theorem 5.1.1 and Remark 5.1.2]). Keep the above notation and
assumptions. The following statements hold.
(1) G = Gaff · Gant ≃ Gaff × Gant /(Gaff ∩ Gant ).
(2) Gaff ∩ Gant contains (Gant )aff .
(3) The quotient (Gaff ∩ Gant )/(Gant )aff is finite.
(4) The multiplication map of G induces an isogeny
                                m : (Gaff × Gant )/(Gant )aff −→ G,
    where (Gant )aff is viewed as a subgroup scheme of Gaff × Gant via x 7→ (x, x−1 ).
6                                                    FEI HU

  The theorem below is a special case of a theorem due to Lucchini Arteche [LA17] which
plays an important role in the proof of our main theorems. It could be regarded as an effective
version of Brion’s theorem on the existence of the quasi-splitness of an extension of algebraic
groups with finite quotient (cf. [Bri15, Theorem 1.1]).
Theorem 2.4 (cf. [LA17, Theorem 3.2]). Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic
p ≥ 0. Let Γ be a smooth finite k-group of order n, and G an arbitrary smooth k-group. Then
for any group extension
                                1 −→ G −→ H −→ Γ −→ 1,
there exist a finite smooth k-subgroup S of G and a commutative diagram with exact rows
                              1      / S
                                             _
                                                      / F
                                                             _
                                                                     / Γ   / 1


                                                       
                              1      / G             / H             / Γ   / 1.

Moreover, if G is an algebraic torus with rank r, then S can be taken as a subgroup of the
n-torsion subgroup G[n] of G. In particular, the order of S divides nr .

                                  3. P ROOFS OF THEOREMS

We are eventually interested only in questions concerning algebraic groups or varieties defined
over algebraically closed fields. So from now on, we will assume that k is algebraically closed.

Proof of Theorem 1.3. We may assume that G is smooth (or equivalently, reduced), since we
only consider finite subgroups of the group G(k) of k-rational points. We first consider the
case that G is connected. In the following Steps 1-3, we will show the theorem under this case.
S TEP 1. Let Gaff and Gant denote the affine part and the anti-affine part of G, respectively (see
§2.2). We claim that Gaff × Gant is generalized p-Jordan. Indeed, since both Gaff and Gant are
generalized p-Jordan, the claim follows from Lemma 2.1(1). More precisely, let n be the least
dimension of a faithful representation of Gaff over k. Then there is a constant J(n) which is
essentially from Theorem 1.1 such that every finite p′ -subgroup Γ of Gaff × Gant contains a
normal abelian subgroup of index ≤ J(n).
S TEP 2. Let N denote (Gant )aff . Consider the following exact sequence of algebraic groups:
                    1 −→ N −→ Gaff × Gant −→ (Gaff × Gant )/N −→ 1.
We claim that the quotient group (Gaff × Gant )/N is generalized p-Jordan. Let Γ be a finite
p′ -subgroup of (Gaff × Gant )/N. Let H be the inverse (or pullback) of the finite group Γ in
Gaff × Gant (cf. [Bri17, Proposition 2.8.3]). Then according to Theorem 2.4, there exist a finite
smooth k-subgroup S of N and a commutative diagram of algebraic groups:
                              1       / S
                                                 _
                                                      / F
                                                                 _
                                                                     / Γ    / 1

                                                                                             (3.1)
                                                        
                              1      / N              / H            / Γ   / 1.
             JORDAN PROPERTY FOR ALGEBRAIC GROUPS AND AUTOMORPHISM GROUPS                             7

  In characteristic zero, there is a normal abelian subgroup AF of F such that [F : AF ] ≤ J(n)
by Step 1. It follows that the image A of AF in Γ is a normal abelian subgroup of Γ of index
[Γ : A] ≤ [F : AF ] ≤ J(n).
   Now we assume that p = char(k) > 0. By [Bri17, Proposition 5.5.1], any anti-affine
group over k is a semi-abelian variety. Thus N = (Gant )aff is an algebraic torus over k. In
particular, N is commutative and so is S. So S(p) is the unique normal Sylow p-subgroup of
S. By the assumption on Γ that p ∤ |Γ|, S(p) is also a Sylow p-subgroup of F . It follows from
S E F that S(p) is also normal in F . Then the Schur–Zassenhaus theorem asserts that there
are complements SC and FC of S(p) = F(p) in S and F respectively; see also the proof of
Lemma 2.2(1). It follows that FC is a p′ -subgroup of Gaff × Gant and hence contains a normal
abelian subgroup AFC of index ≤ J(n) by Step 1 as in the previous case; the rest is the same.

S TEP 3. By Rosenlicht’s decomposition Theorem 2.3, we have the following exact sequence
of algebraic groups:
                                                              m
                          1 −→ K −→ (Gaff × Gant )/N −−→ G −→ 1,                                  (3.2)
where N = (Gant )aff as in Step 2 and K := (Gaff ∩ Gant )/N is a finite group so that m, induced
from the multiplication map of G, is an isogeny. Note that Gant is commutative (cf. [Bri17,
Proposition 3.3.5]). Then K is abelian and hence K(p) is the normal Sylow p-subgroup of K.
Let Γ be a finite p′ -subgroup of G. It follows from Lemma 2.2(1) and Step 2 that Γ contains a
normal abelian subgroup A of index ≤ J(n).

S TEP 4. Finally, with the aid of [Pop11, Lemma 2.11], we are able to deal with non-connected
algebraic groups as well. Indeed, let G◦ be the neutral component of G. Denote by cG the order
of the group π0 (G) := G/G◦ of connected components of G. Then any finite p′ -subgroup Γ of
G contains a normal abelian subgroup A of index ≤ cG J(n)cG , where n is the least dimension
of a faithful representation of (G◦ )aff over k.

  We finally conclude the proof of Theorem 1.3 by letting J(G) = cG J(n)cG .                         

Proof of Theorem 1.7. The proof of Theorem 1.7 basically follows the strategy of the proof of
Theorem 1.3. Note, however, that the group Γ may be of order divisible by p now.
    We first consider the case that G is a connected algebraic group. We may assume that k is
algebraically closed. In Step 1, we have that J ′ (Gaff ) = J ′ (n), e(Gaff ) = 3 by Theorem 1.5, and
J ′ (Gant ) = 1, e(Gant ) = 1 because Gant is commutative (cf. [Bri17, Proposition 3.3.5]). Here n
is the least dimension of a faithful representation of Gaff over k as usual. Thus by Lemma 2.1(2),
J ′ (Gaff × Gant ) = J ′ (Gaff )J ′ (Gant ) = J ′ (n) and e(Gaff × Gant ) = e(Gaff ) + e(Gant ) − 1 = 3.
In other words, any finite subgroup Γ of Gaff × Gant contains a normal abelian p′ -subgroup of
index ≤ J ′ (n) · |Γ(p) |3 .
  Then in Step 2, we claim that any finite subgroup Γ of (Gaff × Gant )/N contains a normal
abelian p′ -subgroup of index ≤ J ′ (n) · |Γ(p) |3(rG +1) , where rG is the rank of the algebraic torus
N = (Gant )aff which is further bounded by the rank of Gaff . Indeed, we follow the argument
8                                                   FEI HU

as in the proof of Theorem 1.3 and get the commutative diagram (3.1). By the previous step,
F contains a normal abelian p′ -subgroup AF of index ≤ J ′ (n) · |F(p) |3 . Note that Theorem 2.4
also yields that the order of S divides |Γ|rG . In particular, |S(p) | divides |Γ(p) |rG . Hence the
image A of AF in Γ is a normal abelian p′ -subgroup of Γ such that
                                                                           3
     [Γ : A] ≤ [F : AF ] ≤ J ′ (n) · |F(p) |3 = J ′ (n) · |S(p) | · |Γ(p) | ≤ J ′ (n) · |Γ(p) |3(rG +1) ,

as claimed.
  In Step 3, we consider the exact sequence (3.2). Recall that K := (Gaff ∩ Gant )/N is a finite
group (depending on G canonically). Let Γ be a finite subgroup of G. Then it follows from the
previous step and Lemma 2.2(2) that Γ contains a normal abelian p′ -subgroup A of index

                             [Γ : A] ≤ J ′ (n) · |K(p) |3(rG +1) · |Γ(p) |3(rG +1) .

  Lastly, we consider the case that G may be non-connected. As before, let π0 (G) = G/G◦
denote the group of connected components of G and cG = |π0 (G)|. Then any finite subgroup
Γ of G contains a normal abelian p′ -subgroup A of index at most
                                                 cG
         ′            3(rG +1)           3(rG +1)
   cG J (n) · |K(p) |          · |Γ(p) |              = cG J ′ (n)cG · |K(p) |3(rG +1)cG · |Γ(p) |3(rG +1)cG ,

where n is the least dimension of a faithful representation of (G◦ )aff over k.
  Let J ′ (G) denote cG J ′ (n)cG · |K(p) |3(rG +1)cG and e(G) := 3(rG + 1)cG . We thus complete
the proof of Theorem 1.7.                                                                     

  Given a projective variety X defined over k, the automorphism group scheme AutX of
X is locally of finite type over k and the automorphism group Aut(X) is just the rational
k-points of AutX , i.e., Aut(X) = AutX (k); in particular, the reduced neutral component
(Aut◦X )red of AutX is a smooth algebraic group defined over k (see e.g. [Bri17, §7]). We
denote (Aut◦X )red (k) by Aut◦ (X).

Proof of Theorem 1.9. Let G := (Aut◦X )red and Γ◦ := Γ ∩ Aut◦ (X). Applying Theorem 1.3
to Γ◦ ≤ G(k), there is a normal abelian subgroup AΓ◦ of Γ◦ of index ≤ J(G) = J(n), where
n is the least dimension of a faithful representation of Gaff over k. By [MZ18, Lemma 2.5],
there is a constant ℓX depending only on X such that [Γ : Γ◦ ] ≤ ℓX (note that their proof is
independent of the characteristic; see [MZ18, Remark 2.6]). It follows that
                                                             |Γ/Γ◦ |
                                         \                    \
                                  A :=         g −1AΓ◦ g =             gi−1 AΓ◦ gi
                                         g∈Γ                  i=1

is a normal abelian subgroup of Γ, where gi ’s are representatives of Γ/Γ◦ . Note that gi−1AΓ◦ gi
is a normal abelian group of Γ◦ of index ≤ J(n) for each i. This yields that the index of A in
Γ◦ is at most J(n)ℓX (see also [Pop11, Lemma 2.11]). We thus have

                               [Γ : A] = [Γ : Γ◦ ] · [Γ◦ : A] ≤ ℓX J(n)ℓX .

To conclude the proof, we let JX := ℓX J(n)ℓX .                                                            
               JORDAN PROPERTY FOR ALGEBRAIC GROUPS AND AUTOMORPHISM GROUPS                                      9

Remark 3.1. In fact, using a theorem due to Chermak and Delgado (cf. [Isa08, Theorem 1.41]),
there exists a characteristic (and hence normal) abelian subgroup M of Γ such that
                      [Γ : M] ≤ [Γ : AΓ◦ ]2 = [Γ : Γ◦ ]2 · [Γ◦ : AΓ◦ ]2 ≤ ℓ2X J(n)2 .
Note, however, that the construction of this so-called Chermak–Delgado subgroup M of Γ is
independent of AΓ◦ (see [Isa08, Corollary 1.45]). Thus we do not know whether M is still a
subgroup of AΓ◦ so that this argument breaks down in the proof of Theorem 1.10 (since M may
not be a p′ -subgroup of an arbitrary finite subgroup Γ of G(k)).

Proof of Theorem 1.10. Let G := (Aut◦X )red and Γ◦ := Γ ∩ Aut◦ (X) as above. Then applying
Theorem 1.7 to Γ◦ ≤ G(k), there is a normal abelian p′ -subgroup AΓ◦ of Γ◦ such that
                                    [Γ◦ : AΓ◦ ] ≤ J ′ (G) · |Γ◦(p) |3(rG +1) ,
where Γ◦(p) is the Sylow p-subgroup of Γ◦ and rG is the rank of (Gant )aff . As in the proof of
Theorem 1.9, we also have [Γ : Γ◦ ] ≤ ℓX for some constant ℓX depending only on X. Similarly,
there is a normal abelian p′ -subgroup A of Γ of index
                                                          ℓX
                   ◦    ◦               ′       ◦ 3(rG +1)
     :           :        :
  [Γ A] = [Γ Γ ] · [Γ A] ≤ ℓX J (G) · |Γ(p) |                  ≤ ℓX J ′ (G)ℓX · |Γ(p) |3(rG +1)ℓX .

The corollary follows by letting JX′ := ℓX J ′ (G)ℓX and eX = 3(rG + 1)ℓX .                                     

Remark 3.2. It is known that if an algebraic torus T acting faithfully on an algebraic variety X,
then T acts generically freely on X (cf. [Dem70, §1.6, Corollaire 1]). This yields that
                               rG = rank(Gant )aff ≤ rank Gaff ≤ dim X.

inspiring discussions and valuable comments on an earlier draft. He also thanks De-Qi Zhang
for several helpful suggestions. He is grateful to an anonymous referee for pointing out an
inaccuracy in a former version.
